note.content: Loved how Adiga portrays the duality of India - the Light and the Darkness. Balram's journey from servant to entrepreneur is both disturbing and compelling. The rooster coop metaphor stayed with me.
The epistolary format (letter to Wen Jiabao) was an interesting choice. Made me question the reliability of the narrator. Great discussion on whether Balram's actions were justified.
Reading this for the second time - noticing more details about Swedish corporate culture and the Vanger family dynamics. Lisbeth Salander remains one of the most complex female protagonists.
Austen's wit shines through every page. Elizabeth Bennet's refusal of Mr. Collins was revolutionary for its time. The social commentary on entailment and women's limited options is still relevant.
